To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the comprehension of metaphors requires the construction of mental representations that are distinctively different from those that are used for literal language, (ii) these mental representations are constructed by the activation of a set of mental models that is associated with the target domain of the metaphor, (iii) these mental models are not constructed in a single, unitary way, but rather are constructed in a variety of ways depending upon the nature of the metaphor and the context in which it is presented, (iv
(a) metaphors and similes are not processed in the same way; (b)

the cognitive representation of a metaphor is not a single, unitary entity, but rather a complex, dynamic structure, which includes the literal meaning of the metaphorical expression, the metaphorical interpretation, and the contextual information that is activated in processing the metaphor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nature of the cognitive mechanisms involved in the comprehension of metaphoric language.
the nature, function and development of metaphor in the mind, and with the role that it plays in the acquisition of language and thought.
the nature of metaphors, the way they are used and understood by people, and the way they function in language.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
metaphors are a form of language which are used in order to express feelings, thoughts or ideas which cannot be expressed in literal terms.
metaphor is a complex and multifaceted phenomenon that is best approached from several different perspectives and with several different methodologies.
metaphor is a cognitive mechanism which is used to create a conceptual link between two domains of knowledge.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have been able to show that metaphors are not merely linguistic ornaments, but that they are cognitive tools for thinking and reasoning. metaphor is the cognitive and emotional bridge between two different conceptual worlds, the world of our everyday life and the world of our dreams.
we have been trying to understand the cognitive mechanisms of metaphor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cognitive science of metaphor is a vibrant and rapidly expanding field.

metaphors are processed in a way that is fundamentally similar to literal language: the literal and metaphorical meanings of a sentence are activated in parallel, and the metaphorical meaning can be activated to a high degree without the literal meaning being fully understood.
